message.reasoning_content:
Analyze: kernel computes in FP32 with div_rn. Risk: FP16 extrema — a*c + b*d can overflow FP32? No, FP16 max ~65504, products ~4.3e9, sum ~8.6e9, fine in FP32. But tolerance 1e-7 + 5e-7*|target| is very tight; FP32 computation error may exceed relative 5e-7 due to cancellation in real_numerator (a*c + b*d). Extreme cases: a*c ≈ -b*d catastrophic cancellation → FP32 error relative to small result can blow past tolerance. Also FP32 rounding of scale. Reference FP64. So risk: componentwise tolerance may be unattainable with plain FP32 naive formula when numerator cancellation occurs. Also signed zeros preserved? Real formula gives -0 vs +0 but signed zeros numerically equal. Also other=1 for masked c load, fine.

Also masked loads other values: fine since masked stores.

Record description update.
